# Kyle

A universal task runner that speaks everyone's language. Define tasks in a Kylefile, or use existing Makefiles, justfiles, package.json, Cargo.toml, and more.

## Installation

```bash
curl -fsSL https://kylefile.dev/install.sh | sh
```

Windows:
```powershell
irm https://kylefile.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Quick Start

```toml
# kyle: toml
name = "my-project"

[tasks.build]
desc = "Build the project"
run = "cargo build --release"

[tasks.test]
desc = "Run tests"
run = "cargo test"
deps = ["build"]
```

```bash
kyle          # List tasks
kyle build    # Run build
kyle test     # Runs build first, then test
```

## Kylefile Schema

### TOML

```toml
# kyle: toml
name = "project-name"          # Optional

[tasks.task-name]
desc = "Description"           # Optional
run = "shell command"          # Required
deps = ["other-task"]          # Optional

[includes]
alias = "path/to/dir"         # Optional - register namespaces
```

### YAML

```yaml
name: project-name

tasks:
  task-name:
    desc: Description
    run: shell command
    deps: [other-task]

includes:
  alias: path/to/dir
```

### Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | No | Project name |
| `tasks.<name>.run` | Yes | Shell command to execute |
| `tasks.<name>.desc` | No | Description shown in task list |
| `tasks.<name>.deps` | No | Tasks to run first |
| `includes.<alias>` | No | Path to namespace directory |

## Supported Files

Kyle auto-detects and reads tasks from these files (in priority order):

### Native
- `Kylefile`, `Kylefile.toml`, `Kylefile.yaml`, `Kylefile.yml`

### Parsed (scripts/tasks extracted from file content)
- `Makefile`, `makefile`, `GNUmakefile` — make targets
- `justfile`, `Justfile` — just recipes
- `Taskfile.yml`, `Taskfile.yaml` — go-task tasks
- `Rakefile` — Ruby rake tasks
- `package.json` — npm/bun/pnpm scripts, workspaces supported
- `composer.json` — PHP composer scripts
- `deno.json`, `deno.jsonc` — Deno tasks
- `pyproject.toml` — PDM/Hatch/Rye scripts + PEP-621 `[project.scripts]` console entries

### Standard (common commands generated automatically)
- `Cargo.toml` — build, test, run, check, clippy, fmt
- `go.mod` — build, test, run, vet, fmt
- `pubspec.yaml` — run, build, test, analyze, pub-get
- `*.csproj` — build, test, run, publish, clean
- `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts` — build, test, run, clean
- `pom.xml` — compile, test, package, install, clean
- `CMakeLists.txt` — configure, build, test, clean

## Namespaces

Run tasks in subdirectories:

```bash
kyle backend:build        # Run build in ./backend/
kyle frontend:test        # Run test in ./frontend/
kyle backend.build        # Dot separator also works
kyle apps/mobile:dev      # Nested paths
```

Cross-namespace dependencies:

```toml
[tasks.deploy]
deps = ["backend:build", "frontend:build"]
run = "echo deploying"
```

Namespaces are auto-discovered from subdirectories containing any supported task file.

## Dispatcher Subcommands

Some tasks are "dispatchers" that proxy to an underlying tool with its own subcommands (e.g. Django's `manage.py`, installed via PDM/uv as a console script like `ccm-admin`). Kyle discovers these and exposes the subcommands as first-class tasks.

```bash
kyle exportxml             # Runs Django's manage.py exportxml directly
kyle ccm-admin:exportxml   # Qualified form (always works)
kyle backend:ccm-admin:exportxml  # From a parent directory
```

Resolution:
- Explicit local task shadows dispatcher sub with the same name
- Local level shadows discovered namespaces
- Same-target dispatchers dedupe alphabetically
- Ambiguous matches refuse to run and list qualified forms to pick from

Currently Django is the only built-in dispatcher extension; the trait system accepts future extensions (Rails, artisan, etc.).

## Task Arg Passthrough

`kyle <task> <args...>` passes everything after the task name raw to the task — no `--` separator needed.

```bash
kyle ccm-admin --help          # Django's help
kyle ccm-admin migrate --noinput
kyle echo --flag1 value
```

Kyle only intercepts the first arg when it's a reserved command (`init`, `config`, etc.) or starts with `-`.

## Reserved Command Collisions

If a namespace dir or dispatcher subcommand has the same name as a reserved kyle command, kyle warns at listing time. To invoke it, use the qualified form or the `--dir` escape:

```bash
kyle --dir config:list    # Forces task-route resolution past the reserved 'config'
kyle config:list          # Qualified form also works
```

## MCP Server

Kyle includes a built-in MCP server for AI tool integration.

```bash
kyle mcp              # Start MCP server (stdio)
kyle mcp --config     # Print config JSON for AI clients
```

### Tools

- `list_tasks` — Returns all tasks with names, descriptions, deps, source type, namespace tasks, and dispatcher subcommands grouped by app
- `run_task` — Runs a task by name (supports namespaced tasks and dispatcher subcommands), returns stdout/stderr

### Setup

Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user kyle -- kyle mcp`
Claude Desktop: add to `~/.claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
Cursor: add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`
Windsurf: add to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`
Codex: `codex mcp add kyle -- kyle mcp` or `~/.codex/config.toml`
Antigravity: add to `~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json`
GitHub Copilot: add to `.vscode/mcp.json` (per-project, key is `servers` not `mcpServers`)

JSON config format (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kyle": {
      "command": "kyle",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Codex TOML format (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.kyle]
command = "kyle"
args = ["mcp"]
```

GitHub Copilot format (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "kyle": {
      "command": "kyle",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## CLI Reference

```
kyle                              List available tasks (grouped dispatcher subs shown)
kyle <task> [args...]             Run a task (args passed through raw)
kyle --dir <task> [args...]       Run a task even if it shadows a reserved name
kyle init [name] [--yaml|--toml]  Create a new Kylefile
kyle upgrade                      Upgrade to latest version
kyle upgrade --status             Show recent auto-upgrade activity
kyle mcp                          Start MCP server
kyle mcp --config                 Print MCP config JSON
kyle config list                  Show all settings
kyle config get <key>             Get a setting
kyle config set <key> <value>     Set a setting
kyle config path                  Show config file path
kyle completions <shell>          Generate shell completions (bash, zsh, fish)
kyle version                      Print version
```

## Settings

| Key | Values | Default | Description |
|-----|--------|---------|-------------|
| `default_format` | `toml`, `yaml` | `toml` | Format for `kyle init` |
| `auto_upgrade` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Auto-check for updates |
| `verify_updates` | `true`, `false` | `true` | SHA256 verification on upgrade |
| `autocorrect` | `suggest`, `off`, `autocorrect` | `suggest` | Behavior on mistyped task names |

Config stored at `~/.config/kyle/config.toml`.

## Typo Handling

Kyle detects typos via Damerau-Levenshtein distance against your task list (max 2 edits, 50% match-ratio guard).

- `suggest` (default): prints `Did you mean 'build'?` and exits 1.
- `off`: plain `task not found` error.
- `autocorrect`: prints a stderr notice (`kyle: running 'build' (corrected from 'buld')`) and runs the corrected task. Args are preserved.

Reserved kyle commands (`upgrade`, `config`, etc.) are never auto-targeted. Ambiguous matches degrade to suggest mode regardless of setting.

Tab completion in bash/zsh/fish also falls back to fuzzy matching when no prefix match exists — independent of the `autocorrect` setting.

## Common Patterns

### Zero-config with existing files

```bash
# Any supported file just works:
kyle build    # Cargo.toml? runs cargo build. Makefile? runs make build.
kyle test     # package.json? runs npm run test. go.mod? runs go test.
```

### Task chains

```toml
[tasks.clean]
run = "rm -rf dist/"

[tasks.build]
run = "npm run build"
deps = ["clean"]

[tasks.deploy]
run = "./deploy.sh"
deps = ["build"]
```

Running `kyle deploy` executes: clean -> build -> deploy.
